original_question: Is the uniform subgroup membership problem decidable for(finitely generated free)-by-cyclic groups? That is, for a fixed group G = Fn ⋊ Z, is there an algorithm that, given elements w, h1,..., hk ∈ G, decides whether or not w belongs to the subgroup H = ⟨h1,..., hk ⟩?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.62 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of The Kourovka Notebook.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official formulation almost verbatim. It correctly identifies the class as finitely generated free-by-cyclic groups, correctly specializes to a fixed ambient group G = F_n ⋊ Z, correctly poses the algorithmic membership question for an input element w and subgroup generators h_1, ..., h_k, and correctly names this as the uniform subgroup membership problem.
missing_details: Spell out that F_n denotes a free group of finite rank n.
Spell out that Z is the infinite cyclic group, so the paper is asking about finitely generated free-by-infinite-cyclic groups.
Make explicit that the ambient group G is fixed in advance and is not part of the input; only w and the finite tuple h_1, ..., h_k are input.
Make explicit that k is arbitrary but finite, so H is any finitely generated subgroup of the fixed group G.
refined_question: For a fixed group G = F_n ⋊ Z, where F_n is a free group of finite rank n and Z is the infinite cyclic group, does there exist an algorithm that, given an element w ∈ G and finitely many elements h_1, ..., h_k ∈ G, decides whether w belongs to the subgroup H = ⟨h_1, ..., h_k⟩?
justification: The draft is essentially already the exact statement of Problem 21.62. The paper formulates it as: "Is the uniform subgroup membership problem decidable for (finitely generated free)-by-cyclic groups? That is, for a fixed group G = F_n ⋊ Z, is there an algorithm that, given elements w, h_1, . . . , h_k ∈ G, decides whether or not w belongs to the subgroup H = ⟨h_1, . . . , h_k⟩?" The nearby context shows that Problem 21.61 is a different algorithmic question about finding finite presentations of finitely generated subgroups, and the cross-reference to Archive Problem 4.8 only provides background that finitely generated free-by-cyclic groups, and indeed their finitely generated subgroups, are finitely presented. It is therefore best to keep the refined question narrowly focused on membership, not broaden it to subgroup presentations or other algorithmic problems.
